name_reason: Already conforms to data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: domain=battle (core battle-system table cluster in .object2), descriptor=view_window_max_x reflects both purpose (battle view-window maximum x extent) and that it is a scalar coordinate extent. No Ghidra address residue (no _51a87 suffix; the _x / _max_x tokens are semantic). Sibling y-extent is data_fd2_battle_view_window_max_y @ 0x51A8B.
purpose: Battle view-window maximum x extent, in map tiles (value 13): the rightward span of the on-screen battle camera relative to the window origin.
logic_summary: Single dword scalar (NOT a table), read via absolute-address load. Two distinct uses across 15 readers: (1) Visible-tile/sprite cull -- a world (x,y) is drawn only when origin_x-1 <= x <= origin_x + view_window_max_x (signed comparison), paired 1:1 with the y-extent sibling; (2) Tactical-overview camera in fd2_open_tactical_overview_zoom: src_cx_fp_base = origin_x*0xC00 + view_window_max_x*0x600 (16:6 fixed point), consumed as a full 32-bit integer. Verified readers fd2_blit_animated_tile_at_pos @ 0x12AE9 (bounds check) and fd2_open_tactical_overview_zoom @ 0x2007B (fixed-point camera math).
element_semantics: Single 32-bit value = 13. Acts as a non-negative coordinate extent in the visible cull (always small positive, signed compares) and as a plain 32-bit operand in the tactical-overview fixed-point camera arithmetic.
comment_original_issue: The home-file block was accurate and precise, but the line directly above the declaration read '/* Non-const: read-only in-game, but tests set the window extent as a fixture. */' while the declaration is 'const uint32'. That annotation contradicted the actual (correct) const declaration; the symbol has zero game-side writers (all 15 xrefs are READ), so it is genuinely read-only and const is correct.
notes: Removed the contradictory '/* Non-const: ... */' comment line above the declaration (const is correct: 0 game-side writers). const keyword/type/value/declaration otherwise unchanged. Created a concise Ghidra data PLATE_COMMENT (previously empty) summarizing the scalar's role, the two use sites, and the read-only status; content consistent with the src block. No logic touched.
